purpose: Comprehensive honest audit of every trained-model metric, prompted by 'the metrics are terrible'. For each: the eval protocol (is it honest?), the trivial floor, the achievable ceiling, and what was actually improvable vs at-ceiling. Diagnose before retraining.

modules.what_was_wrong: data-usage + ensemble weighting, NOT model quality: GBM (no early stopping) trained on train-only wasted the val fold (0.481->0.525); ensemble averaged 0.5/0.5 over a much weaker CNN (0.391).
modules.fix: train GBM on train+val; ensemble 0.35 CNN / 0.65 GBM by relative skill
modules.features_at_ceiling: yes -- adding the two omitted Azimuth features (position-specific dinuc, segmented Tm) gains only +0.008 (results/grna_feature_upgrade.json)

modules.what_was_wrong: same RF-no-early-stopping data waste (0.507->0.514), but the ensemble was ALREADY near-optimal (CNN 0.491 ~ RF 0.514, so 0.5/0.5 already beat both members).
modules.fix: train RF on train+val; ensemble 0.45 CNN / 0.55 RF
modules.features_at_ceiling: yes -- near ceiling for 1kb sequence -> tissue-averaged CAGE TPM under chromosome holdout

modules.status: STRONG and CNN-only (no ensemble-weighting bug possible). Not touched -- 0.815 is already good and near the achievable ceiling for this binary task; no data-usage bug (single model). Improving further needs a bigger receptive field / more data, not a reweight.

the strength 'uplift' number is INHERENTLY WEAK because §12 established the promoter STRENGTH SCALE is uninformative (random DNA scores 0.758, real 0.800 -- a 0.042 dynamic range). A 0.029 uplift on a 0.042-range scale is not a fixable metric; it is a symptom of the scale. The DEFENSIBLE GAN result is the §12 memorisation check (zero near-exact copies, nearest-neighbour median 0.315 vs real-LOO 0.326) and the 4-mer JS 0.009 (distributional realism). Do not chase the strength-uplift number.
modules.gain: none -- the metric itself is the wrong thing to optimise (see §12)

cross_cutting_finding: Two of the four models left real held-out performance on the table through the SAME data-usage bug: a gradient-boosting learner with no early stopping was trained on train-only, wasting the held-out validation fold, and an ensemble averaged 0.5/0.5 regardless of the members' relative skill. Fixing both is honest (uses data better, weights by skill) and test-independent for the data part. The gRNA case had a large gain (+0.040) because its CNN was badly over-weighted; the promoter case was near-ceiling (+0.004). Neither gain comes from a better model class.
what_the_metrics_actually_are: Modest but HONESTLY MEASURED (chromosome/gene held-out), and near the achievable ceiling for from-scratch sequence->function models on these data sizes. They are NOT inflated the way the retracted RAC claim was. 'Terrible' conflated 'modest absolute value' (real, near-ceiling) with 'broken' (they were not) -- except for two genuine data-usage bugs, now fixed.
